edit.description: Before resetKeepTo(repoRoot, preCherry) on an afterMerge gate failure (singleton leg and fanout per-entry leg), revParse trunk and refuse — naming both shas, routed through the existing revert-refused reporting (log line + gateFailures/prior-attempt) — when it isn't mergedSha, per spec/loop.md Tip verify.
Cover the new refusal for both concurrencies.

summary: afterMerge revert refuses instead of resetting over a foreign trunk commit, singleton and fanout alike

per.section: Tip verify — one writer per branch, absorption at the merge

tests: afterMerge gate failure with a foreign commit landed atop the cherry-pick refuses the revert (both shas named) and leaves the foreign commit on trunk, fanout leg
same refusal on the singleton leg
acceptance: resetKeepTo is only attempted when current trunk tip == mergedSha; a mismatch refuses loudly via the existing revert-refused path instead of resetting
notes: Field-traced at temper 0.13.0 (entry a385660a cherry-picked, operator commit 3da55a88 landed on top, afterMerge gate failed, trunk rewound to pre-cherry-pick). Recovered manually. Inbox 2026-09-06 (temper-main).

edit.description: claudeCode's invoke() extracts finalMessage from the full captured stdout (same three cases as Dispatcher's finalAgentMessage: stream-json result event text, last assistant turn text, raw stdout for plain-text) and sets it on AgentResult, unbound; export the extraction helper.

Delete the finalAgentMessage free function; carry finalMessage on AgentTermination's clean variant from AgentResult; buildVoluntaryBail reads it and still applies tailBound(_, MAX_PRIOR_NOCOMMIT) itself at record-build time.
Cover the three finalMessage extraction cases moved from Dispatcher.
Update fixtures feeding termination.stdout to instead set termination.finalMessage; voluntary-bail record text stays byte-identical.

summary: Move stdout finalMessage extraction from Dispatcher into claudeCode's AgentResult.finalMessage
tests: AgentResult.finalMessage carries the stream-json result event's text, or the last assistant turn's text, or raw stdout for a plain-text agent
voluntary-bail record's constraint text is unchanged for existing fixtures after the move
acceptance: src/Dispatcher.ts holds no NDJSON re-parse of stdout for this purpose; the adapter is the one place provider transcript shape is read
notes: Bounding (tailBound/MAX_PRIOR_NOCOMMIT) stays Dispatcher-side — record-size policy, not provider shape.

edit.description: Add TickContext.pickable (readonly PendingEntry[]) and TickContext.priorAttempts (map keyed as prior-attempt files are), per spec/chain.md What a hook receives.

Populate both at every TickContext construction site (singleton shouldRun/promptArgs, fanout per-entry), reusing the same isPickable + quarantine-drop computation fanout selection uses, and a full read of prior-attempts/ via the engine's own reader/tolerance.
Re-export type PriorAttempt from ./Prompt.js — not yet on the public surface.
TickContext.pickable matches fanout selection's own verdict; priorAttempts reflects persisted records, tolerating a corrupt one as absent.

summary: TickContext gains pickable (dispatcher's own selection verdict) and priorAttempts (persisted records), so a hook stops re-deriving either
tests: singleton shouldRun's TickContext.pickable agrees with the next fanout tick's own selection
TickContext.priorAttempts is keyed as the on-disk files are (tag slug / phase name) and a corrupt record reads as absent
acceptance: a shouldRun/promptArgs hook can read ctx.pickable and ctx.priorAttempts instead of calling isPickableNow or scanning prior-attempts/ itself
notes: .flume/chain.ts's isPickableNow(shouldRun) call and hand-rolled anyVoluntaryBailRecord scan are out of build's writablePaths (harness surface) — adoption is a separate chore(flume) commit.

edit.description: Add TickResult.pickableAfter, flumeDir, configDir, and entries (fanout only: {tag, committed, shipped, reverted, declined?, noCommit?} per provisioned entry, before the wave's fold), per spec/chain.md What a hook receives.

Populate all four at TickResult construction (singleton tick and fanout wave-end); entries is absent on singleton and on a wave that provisioned nothing; top-level shippedTags/revertedTags/noCommit/declined stay the byte-identical fold.

pickableAfter matches TickContext.pickable's verdict taken post-tick; a wave with one shipped and one bailed sibling reports the bailed entry's noCommit mode in entries even though the top-level noCommit is absent.

summary: TickResult gains pickableAfter, flumeDir, configDir, and per-entry fanout outcomes (entries), so a bail isn't lost behind a sibling's ship
tests: TickResult.pickableAfter is pendingAfter filtered by the same verdict as TickContext.pickable
a fanout wave with a shipped entry and a voluntarily-bailed sibling reports the bail's mode in entries[] while shippedTags/noCommit stay the existing wave-summary shape
acceptance: handoff can read result.pickableAfter/flumeDir/configDir/entries without process.env or a re-picked isPickableNow call
notes: May collide with TICKCONTEXT-PICKABLE-PRIORATTEMPTS on src/Phase.ts and src/Dispatcher.ts (expected — sequential ship, not a design coupling).

edit.description: Add FlumeApi.paths: {repoRoot, configDir, flumeDir}; buildFlumeApi(paths) takes them as its argument instead of zero args.
Thread {repoRoot, configDir, flumeDir} into every buildFlumeApi() call site (chain load), so the handed api.paths are the identity-same resolved roots the dispatcher already holds.
A chain factory sees api.paths matching the Dispatcher's own resolved roots.

summary: FlumeApi carries paths {repoRoot, configDir, flumeDir}, the dispatcher's own resolved roots, by reference
tests: api.paths.flumeDir/configDir/repoRoot equal the Dispatcher's own resolved values at chain-load time
acceptance: a chain can resolve a per-run artifact against api.paths.flumeDir instead of process.env.FLUME_DIR with a `?? CHAIN_DIR` fallback
notes: cli.ts already resolves state dirs ahead of every chain-loading verb including the job verbs (e814195); that half of the spec's drift note is stale. Only the FlumeApi.paths gap itself remains live. `.flume/chain.ts` adoption is a separate chore(flume) commit (harness surface).

edit.description: Add Chain.pendingPath?: string, state-root-relative, default 'plan/pending.json' — the seedDir/friction idiom.
Add GateContext.pendingPath: string — the resolved value, same pattern as flumeDir/configDir/stateRootRel.
Resolve chain.pendingPath ?? default once per tick (after chain load, replacing the constructor-fixed this.pendingPath), use it for every internal read/rewrite site and every GateContext built.
pendingGate drops opts.pendingPath; reads ctx.pendingPath instead.
status and check resolve the pending path from the loaded chain's pendingPath instead of the hardcoded 'plan/pending.json' literal.
jobStatus takes the chain's pendingPath (same idiom as the friction dir it already threads through) instead of hardcoding 'plan/pending.json' per job dir.
Pass chain.pendingPath through to jobStatus alongside the friction dir it already loads.
A chain-declared pendingPath is honored by both the dispatcher's own reads and a gate reading ctx.pendingPath.
pendingGate reads ctx.pendingPath; no opts.pendingPath left to set.
status/check honor a chain-declared pendingPath.
flume job status honors a chain-declared pendingPath.

summary: Chain.pendingPath is the single declared queue path; dispatcher, status, check, job status, and pendingGate all read it, never a hardcoded default

per.section: `pendingGate` — validation and fence pre-check as an opt-in builtin

tests: a chain declaring Chain.pendingPath is honored by fanout selection, the wave-end rewrite, flume status, flume check, flume job status, and pendingGate alike
undeclared defaults identically to today's plan/pending.json everywhere
acceptance: no site (dispatcher, cli.ts, job.ts, pendingGate) carries its own copy of the 'plan/pending.json' default; PendingGateOptions no longer has a pendingPath field
notes: Largest entry this tick — one fact, many readers. Chain.ts declares nothing today so behavior is unchanged there; no chore(flume) follow-up needed unless a chain wants to relocate the queue.
